instruction:
Fix `plugins/catalog/src/components/CatalogEntityPage/useEntityFromUrl.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. FIX (user item 4). The hook returns `loading: isLookupLoading`, which is false once the DIRECT lookup settles — but the former-ref resolution query runs AFTER that. So for a stale ref the hook briefly reports {loading: false, entity: undefined}, the not-found panel flashes, and only then the redirect happens.

Keep `loading` true until the former-ref resolution has SETTLED, and — when it resolved to an entity — until the navigation actually happens. Requirements, all of which must hold simultaneously:

  (a) A ref that resolves directly must be UNAFFECTED: no extra loading, no extra request. The resolution step already short-circuits for that case.
  (b) A stale ref must report loading continuously from the direct lookup through resolution and navigation, so the not-found panel never flashes.
  (c) A resolution that settles as UNRESOLVED must RELEASE loading and let the ordinary not-found panel render — it must never leave the page loading forever. This includes the resolution erroring.
  (d) The anti-loop guards from the design must keep working: the `attemptedRefRef` guard (resolution attempted at most once per requested ref) and the `navigatedRefRef` guard must not be defeated or bypassed, and the destination ref — where the direct lookup succeeds — must never enter resolution.
  (e) The existing no-flash-on-navigation behaviour must be preserved: the `isStale` window where `lookupResult` belongs to a previous ref still reads as loading (this is what keeps plugins/catalog/src/alpha/pages.test.tsx 'does not flash Entity not found when navigating to another entity' passing — do not regress it).

A workable derivation is to treat loading as `isLookupLoading || (resolutionIsPending-for-this-ref) || (resolutionResolved && navigation-not-yet-performed-for-this-ref)`, where the pending notion is keyed on the requested ref so a settled-unresolved outcome releases it. Use whatever minimal correct form satisfies (a)-(e).

Change nothing else: keep the guarded ref stringification that must not throw when `kind` is absent, the sub-path/query/fragment prefix swap, the errorApi 'No name provided!' path, and the returned shape `{ entity, loading, error, refresh }`. EXISTING file — keep its Apache 2.0 header year unchanged.

instruction:
Fix `docs/features/software-catalog/well-known-annotations.md` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. FIX (user item 6). Document two adopter-relevant limitations of the former-entity-refs annotation that are currently undocumented.

In the section covering `backstage.io/former-entity-refs`, add clear prose stating:

  1. **The live-entity and contested checks are viewer-relative.** Former-ref resolution runs through the same permissioned catalog lookup as any other read, so the 'a live entity holding the name always wins' rule and the 'a name claimed by two or more entities resolves to nothing' rule only consider entities THE VIEWER IS PERMITTED TO READ. A viewer who cannot read the entity that really holds a name may therefore be redirected by another entity's claim on it. This is a deliberate consequence of not using a privileged lookup: it is what guarantees the redirect never reveals an entity the viewer may not read. Write this for adopters deciding whether to rely on the feature, in plain language.
  2. **Long refs are ignored.** A former ref is indexed under a synthetic search key built from the annotation name plus the full ref, and the catalog drops search keys longer than 200 characters. In practice a former ref longer than about 147 characters is silently ignored and will not redirect.

Follow the repo's documentation style guide at docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md and match this file's existing heading levels, table/prose conventions and tone exactly. Keep every other annotation entry byte-identical. Do not reference internal code symbols (function names, class names, variable names, file paths) — write for adopters in terms of observable behaviour. Return the WHOLE file.
